top_stories.title: US summons bank bosses over cyber risks from Anthropic's latest AI model
top_stories.summary: US authorities have summoned senior banking executives to discuss cybersecurity risks posed by Anthropic's latest AI model, in an unusual intervention highlighting concerns about frontier AI systems in critical financial infrastructure. The Guardian reports the move signals growing regulatory attention to the security implications of advanced AI deployments. The development follows Wired's reporting that Anthropic's Mythos model could force a broader cybersecurity reckoning.

top_stories.title: Anthropic's Mythos Will Force a Cybersecurity Reckoning—Just Not the One You Think
top_stories.summary: Wired reports that Anthropic's new Mythos AI model raises significant cybersecurity questions, though the implications may differ from the obvious concerns about AI being used to attack systems. The piece argues the reckoning is less about direct offensive capability and more about how AI changes the broader threat landscape for security practitioners. The analysis adds context to the US government's decision to convene banking executives over the model's risks.

top_stories.title: Scientists invented a fake disease. AI told people it was real
top_stories.summary: Nature reports on an experiment in which researchers created a fictitious medical condition and found that AI systems confidently told users the fake disease was real, raising serious concerns about AI reliability in health information contexts. The findings illustrate the risks of AI-generated misinformation in sensitive domains where accuracy is critical. The study adds to debate around AI bias, hallucination, and the safety of AI health tools.

top_stories.title: Elon Musk released xAI's Grok 4 without any safety reports—despite calling AI more 'dangerous than nukes'
top_stories.summary: xAI released Grok 4 without publishing any safety evaluation reports, according to reporting linked via Google News, despite Elon Musk's own public statements describing AI as potentially more dangerous than nuclear weapons. The move draws scrutiny over the consistency between Musk's safety rhetoric and xAI's actual transparency practices. The story adds to broader industry debate about voluntary safety commitments and disclosure standards.

top_stories.title: Fear and loathing at OpenAI
top_stories.summary: The Verge podcast examines the deepening internal tensions and external drama at OpenAI, covering the latest developments including cultural unease, strategic uncertainty, and the broader implications for the company's trajectory. The episode follows a week of significant controversy around OpenAI's leadership and public positioning. It provides context on how internal dynamics are shaping one of the most consequential AI organisations in the world.

further_links.title: The Download: an exclusive Jeff VanderMeer story and AI models too scary to release
further_links.summary: MIT Technology Review's daily briefing covers AI models that labs have deemed too dangerous to publicly release, alongside an exclusive science fiction story exploring AI themes.

further_links.title: Meta's New AI Asked for My Raw Health Data—and Gave Me Terrible Advice
further_links.summary: Wired's hands-on review of Meta's new AI assistant found it solicited sensitive personal health data and then provided advice that experts would consider harmful or misleading.

further_links.title: AI Podcasters Really Want to Tell You How to Keep a Man Happy
further_links.summary: Wired investigates how AI-generated podcast content is proliferating with regressive relationship advice and gender stereotypes, raising questions about algorithmic bias and content moderation.

further_links.title: This Startup Wants You to Pay Up to Talk With AI Versions of Human Experts
further_links.summary: Wired reports on Onix, a startup building a platform where users pay to converse with AI versions of real human experts in fields including therapy, medicine, and nutrition.

further_links.title: OpenAI's response to the Axios developer tool compromise
further_links.summary: OpenAI has published an official statement detailing its response to a security compromise affecting an Axios developer tool, outlining the steps taken to address the incident.

further_links.title: AI assistance when contributing to the Linux kernel
further_links.summary: The official Linux kernel documentation has been updated with guidance on the use of AI coding assistants when contributing code, setting out expectations and limitations for developers using these tools.

further_links.title: How agentic AI is changing enterprise applications [Q&A]
further_links.summary: A Q&A examines how the shift toward agentic AI systems is transforming enterprise software, with expert perspectives on deployment challenges and business impact.

further_links.title: Microsoft starts removing Copilot buttons from Windows 11 apps
further_links.summary: Microsoft has begun removing dedicated Copilot buttons from Windows 11 applications, signalling a shift in how the company plans to integrate AI assistant functionality into its operating system.

further_links.title: The Iranian Lego AI video creators credit their virality to 'heart'
further_links.summary: The Verge follows up on the viral pro-Iran AI Lego video phenomenon, interviewing creators who say emotional resonance rather than technical sophistication drove their content's spread.

further_links.title: 20-year-old man arrested for allegedly throwing a Molotov cocktail at Sam Altman's house
further_links.summary: A 20-year-old man has been arrested for allegedly attacking the San Francisco home of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman with a Molotov cocktail, in an incident that highlights growing tensions around AI leadership figures.
